facts.label: Bottom line

Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- No executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied, so covenant definitions, baskets and the covenant EBITDA are not available and the first lien leverage covenant cannot be tested or its headroom stated; the debt terms in the debt table rest on the issuer's own note summary. Obtain the executed agreements and their amendments, including the January 22, 2026 repricing. Severity: High. - The statements are consolidated and no separate financial information exists for the borrower, the guarantors or the restricted group, so leverage and cover cannot be read at the level where the debt sits and the revolver covenant is tested. Obtain guarantor or restricted-group financial information if the filer provides it. Severity: High. - The maturity ladder is printed at December 31, 2025 and not at September 30, 2026, so the maturities chart and the principal reconciliation are drawn at year-end and do not show the USD 188 million of principal repaid since. Obtain the ladder at the latest date from the executed agreements or the next filing. Severity: Medium. - The issuer prints no unadjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA (Reported) is calculated here from net income, tax, interest and depreciation, amortization and impairments, which keeps other income and loss on debt financing inside it; interim leverage and cover use twelve-month figures built from unaudited stubs. State the definition beside every ratio and prefer audited year-end columns for conclusions. Severity: Medium. - Cash interest paid is timing-sensitive: the third quarter of 2026 shows USD 63 million against USD 89 million a year earlier, so cover on cash interest of 3.97x is higher than cover on interest expense of 3.48x. Read the two together until a full year of the 2033 notes' April and October coupons is in the data. Severity: Medium. - The adjusted EBITDA add-backs are the issuer's own labels; restructuring and other includes legal and related costs of USD 79 million in 2024, USD 130 million in 2025 and USD 50 million in the first nine months of 2026, and the issuer states no realisation status for any add-back. Obtain the issuer's analysis of which costs it expects not to recur. Severity: Medium. - The financing and investing lines that print a dash in a filing, for example the Q3 2026 loss on debt financing, the Q1 2026 exchange rate effect, the first-quarter and half-year 2026 treasury stock lines and several debt issuance and repayment lines, are carried as missing and not as zero, although the totals show they are nil; no later filing can change this. Severity: Low. - Lines that a quarterly filing does not print, such as proceeds from notes and term loans in the first quarter, are shown as not printed; the annual statements itemise cash flow adjustments that the quarterly statements show in one line, so the annual columns carry calculated sums. Use the sums only for comparison with interim columns. Severity: Low. - Per-share amounts, share counts, noncontrolling interest and discontinued operations are not carried in the statement tables, which state one unit of USD millions; they are in the filings if needed. Severity: Low. - Operating indicator definitions, including average daily revenue per unit and the installed base inclusive of Grover, were revised in the fourth quarter of 2025, so indicators in the 2024 annual report are on the earlier basis. Use the revised comparatives. Severity: Low. - The note maturity day and month, the interest rate floors, and the security and rank of USD 5 million of other debt are not stated in the pages read; the debt stack leaves the other debt out for that reason. Obtain the indentures and credit agreements. Severity: Low. - The Q4 2025 quarter is not printed alone; the 2025 annual report gives only the year, so Q4 2025 would be the difference between FY2025 and the first nine months of 2025. The issuer's 2025 quarterly reports were not supplied, so 2025 interim figures are the comparatives printed in the 2026 reports. Severity: Low. - No supplier finance, factoring, securitisation, customer deposit or deferred revenue arrangement was found in a search of all eight sources, so no non-debt funding float is flagged; contract liabilities are the only related balance and are small. Severity: Low.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a medium rating is behavioural: no dividend has ever been paid, no liability management transaction is described, the 2033 refinancing cut the coupon, revolver borrowings were only USD 70 million against USD 1.0 billion of commitments, repurchases paused in the third quarter, and the issuer reports net debt leverage of 3.3x on its own measure, down from 3.4x. A proxy statement showing an independent board and no related-party dealings, together with tight restricted-payment limits in the executed agreements, would move the rating to low. It would move to high if repurchases resumed before the 3.0x target is reached, if another debt-funded acquisition followed Grover, or if an amendment loosened payment limits. Gaming machine sales also rose 5.29% in the third quarter after falling over nine months, which hints at a recovering replacement cycle for the business that carries group earnings. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case for a better view is deleveraging momentum and earnings quality: principal fell USD 188 million since year-end, the issuer's net debt leverage fell from 3.5x to 3.3x with a target below 3.0x in the first half of 2027, adjusted EBITDA rose 3.81%, the revolver is almost undrawn, and the 2033 notes refinanced at a lower coupon. That case wins if legal costs fall back toward the USD 79 million of 2024, social casino stabilises, the buyback pause holds and the 2029 maturities are addressed well before the Term Loan B nears maturity. The view would turn more cautious if revenue fell again after Q3, if revolver borrowings approached USD 300 million, if repurchases resumed before the target is met, or if a debt-funded acquisition followed Grover. Recurring or leased revenue supports visibility, while sales of machines and systems add cyclicality, so the model supports debt service capacity but not a steady growth path.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10–15, 149; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14

facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: The company is publicly traded as depositary interests on the ASX since November 2025 and quoted over the counter in the United States; no sponsor or controlling holder is named, and holder percentages and board composition sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied. All reported debt sits in a wholly owned subsidiary, Light and Wonder International, Inc., guaranteed by the parent and by wholly owned domestic subsidiaries and secured on first-priority liens for the credit facilities, while the notes are senior unsecured and structurally behind the liabilities of non-guarantor subsidiaries, whose size is not disclosed. Without a sponsor, leverage tolerance is judged from actions: repurchases since 2024, a debt-funded acquisition and a pause in repurchases in the third quarter of 2026. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 62, 100, 169; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is driven by leased machine volumes and daily fees, new machine shipments, social casino payer numbers and iGaming wagers. Gaming operations revenue rose 17.63% and iGaming rose 14.75% in nine months while SciPlay fell 9.68% and machine sales fell 8.18%; services revenue, which carries the leased and digital lines, was 73.52% of revenue and rose 5.90% (calculation CALC-8). Revenue is therefore recurring and visible in the leased and iGaming lines, cyclical in machine and systems sales, and structurally declining in social casino so far; pricing power is shown only by a higher average sales price per new unit in Q3 2026, and no customer concentration is disclosed. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10, 14, 46, 51; calculation CALC-8

facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Costs are largely fixed in the short run: selling, general and administrative costs were USD 869 million in FY2025 against USD 872 million in FY2024 while revenue rose 3.95%, research and development was 7.60% of revenue and depreciation, amortization and impairments 12.25% (calculation CALC-9). Operating leverage therefore helps when revenue grows and hurts when it falls, and cost of products fell {pct(483 - 436, 483)}% against a {pct(1083 - 1017, 1083)}% fall in products revenue, which cushions a cyclical downturn only in part. Margins can be defended under mild volume pressure, but a fall in machine sales with fixed costs would reduce margins faster than revenue. Tariffs and components sourced from China and Asia are a further cost risk the issuer is monitoring. facts.label: Capital intensity and cash flow conversion
facts.text: Capital expenditures were USD 247 million in nine months, 10.12% of revenue, of which Gaming USD 201 million, and operating cash flow was 64.71% of unadjusted EBITDA for nine months against 73.18% in FY2025 (calculation CALC-10), so conversion is good but lower in the period with the settlements. Operating cash flow less capital expenditures was USD 596 million over twelve months (calculation CALC-2), enough to cover scheduled 2026 principal and interest of USD 369 million 1.62x (calculation CALC-4). Gaming operations need heavy up-front capital, so growth in leased units lowers free cash flow before it raises it, and capital spending can be slowed to protect cash if needed, at the cost of installed base growth. facts.label: Porter's Five Forces, credit-translated
facts.text: Rivalry is intense in every segment: the issuer names Aristocrat, IGT and Konami in machines and systems, Playtika and others in social casino and Evolution, Pragmatic Play and Playtech in iGaming, so share losses in a segment hit pricing and the margin that supports debt service. New entrants are a threat mainly in social casino, which the issuer calls a business with low barriers to entry, so SciPlay's margin is the least protected. Substitutes are other forms of play and leisure that compete for player time, which pressures social casino user numbers. facts.label: SWOT, credit-translated
facts.text: Strengths: recurring leased and iGaming earnings, large liquidity, a single first lien covenant and market access shown by the 2033 notes. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: In the next 12 to 24 months the issuer expects full-year adjusted EBITDA growth toward the lower end of a mid-to-high single digit range, a seasonally strong fourth quarter and net debt leverage toward 3.0x by the end of FY2026 and below it in the first half of 2027; scheduled principal is small at USD 53 million in 2026 and USD 63 million in 2027, and the swaps end in April 2027. Tailwinds are installed base growth, Grover expansion and iGaming content; headwinds are social casino weakness, delayed customer investment, legal settlements and higher duties. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: A realistic downside starts with casino operators delaying capital spending, which the issuer already cites, while social casino keeps shrinking at the nine-month pace. Gaming machine sales and systems, 29.06% of revenue, fall first, and fixed costs turn that into a faster fall in adjusted EBITDA; a 10% fall in adjusted EBITDA would lift the issuer's leverage ratio to 3.62x and unadjusted net leverage to 4.88x (calculation CALC-15). Cash flow after capital expenditures would still cover scheduled 2026 debt service 1.21x even if the whole shortfall reached cash, liquidity of USD 1,059 million would remain above the USD 859 million of principal due before 2029, and the revolver's test would apply only after borrowings pass USD 300 million, although the Term Loan A test applies every quarter and its headroom is not established. Management levers are pausing repurchases, slowing capital spending and timing legal settlements, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis, and the pressure falls on refinancing the 2028 and 2029 maturities at a higher spread if leverage stays above the target when the hedge has ended. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 40; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-12; calculation CALC-13

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Light & Wonder presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring leased and iGaming earnings, large liquidity and a stated priority on deleveraging, but credit quality is constrained by leverage that is high on unadjusted earnings, a concentrated 2029 maturity wall and discretionary shareholder returns. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: operating cash flow less capital expenditures covers scheduled debt service 1.62x after legal settlements. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on reaching the leverage target before the 2028 and 2029 maturities and on market conditions when the swaps end. The primary downside path is a casino capital-spending pause with continued social casino decline, followed by weaker earnings against a concentrated maturity wall. Further analysis would require the executed debt agreements, the proxy statement, guarantor information, agency ratings, market pricing and a peer comparison. Top risk: refinancing the 2029 maturities if deleveraging stalls. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-11

## Findings
### Bottom line

The eight supplied filings and earnings releases give a current, consolidated record of Light & Wonder's accounts and debt through September 30, 2026, enough for a credit snapshot, but creditors cannot test covenant, control or rating questions from them.

Every document is dated on or before November 4, 2026, ahead of the November 18, 2026 cutoff, and together they cover two fiscal years and three quarters of 2026. The debt sits at a wholly owned subsidiary and is guaranteed by the parent and its domestic subsidiaries, yet no borrower-group or guarantor financial statements were supplied, so leverage can only be read on the consolidated perimeter. Covenant levels rest on the issuer's own summary in the annual report because no executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied, and ownership and board detail sits in a proxy statement that is not in the supplied set.

## Findings
### Bottom line

On unadjusted earnings, net debt was 4.24x EBITDA at September 30, 2026, well above the 3.3x the issuer reports on adjusted earnings, so creditors should size the risk on the higher figure while recognising that it has fallen from 4.60x at the end of 2025.

The fall came from a USD 182 million cut in carrying debt and from earnings growth, and available liquidity of USD 1,059 million leaves no near-term funding pressure. The gap between the two measures rests on USD 244 million of restructuring and other costs over twelve months, of which legal costs have recurred, and the USD 2,568 million due in 2029 is the next refinancing test.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 21, 54; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 18; calculation CALC-34; calculation CALC-42; calculation CALC-32; calculation CALC-46
### Key findings

- Unadjusted leverage jumped in 2025 and has since eased. Net debt was 3.42x unadjusted EBITDA at the end of 2024, 4.60x at the end of 2025 and 4.24x at September 30, 2026, because carrying debt rose by USD 1,293 million in 2025 while the issuer spent USD 861 million on acquisitions, chiefly Grover, and USD 880 million on share repurchases, and unadjusted EBITDA barely moved, from USD 1,075 million to USD 1,085 million. Since the year-end, carrying debt has fallen by USD 182 million and face value by USD 188 million, USD 153 million of it in the third quarter.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 140–142, 166; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 21; calculation CALC-53; calculation CALC-34; calculation CALC-35; calculation CALC-36; calculation CALC-2

- The issuer's lower leverage rests on add-backs, and the largest recurs. Adjusted EBITDA for the twelve months to September 30, 2026 was USD 1,498 million, USD 355 million above the unadjusted USD 1,143 million, and restructuring and other accounted for USD 244 million of the gap. Legal and related costs inside that line were USD 79 million in 2024, USD 130 million in 2025 and USD 179 million over the last twelve months, so a measure that excludes them flatters the debt a creditor must service in cash.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 148, 154; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 18; calculation CALC-31; calculation CALC-32; calculation CALC-33

- Cash generation improved but is flattered by timing. Operating cash flow was USD 616 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 475 million, USD 141 million more, and after capital expenditures of USD 247 million it left USD 369 million against USD 257 million. The nine-month figure also benefits from USD 137 million of legal settlements all paid in the first quarter that the issuer adds back to its own measure and from USD 46 million released from restricted cash, which counts in the issuer's free cash flow but not in operating cash flow.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 56–57; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_lnw03312026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 18; EX-99.1_2026-08-04_lnw06302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation CALC-37; calculation CALC-38; calculation CALC-39; calculation CALC-40

- Interest cover looks stronger on cash than on expense. Cash interest paid was USD 288 million over the last twelve months, for cover of 3.97x on unadjusted EBITDA, but interest expense was USD 328 million, for cover of 3.48x. The gap probably reflects payment timing: the third quarter shows cash interest of only USD 63 million against USD 89 million a year earlier, and the 2033 notes pay on April 1 and October 1, so the October payment falls outside the third quarter.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 167; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; calculation CALC-29; calculation CALC-30; calculation CALC-54

- Liquidity is adequate and the first large maturity is in 2029. Cash of USD 139 million and undrawn revolver commitments of USD 920 million gave USD 1,059 million at September 30, 2026, against USD 927 million at year-end, with USD 70 million drawn on a USD 1,000 million revolver that matures in 2030. At year-end the principal due in 2029 was USD 2,568 million, the Term Loan B of USD 2,068 million and the 2029 notes of USD 500 million, which is about half of USD 5,207 million of principal, and the ladder has not been printed since.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 54; 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 125, 165–166; calculation CALC-42; calculation CALC-43; calculation CALC-46; calculation CALC-45

- Capital returns and a thin equity base weigh on creditors. The issuer spent USD 193 million on share repurchases and trust purchases in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 380 million a year earlier, with no repurchases under the program in the third quarter, and total equity of USD 423 million is small beside goodwill and intangible assets of USD 4,053 million. No supplier finance, factoring or deposit float was found, and contract liabilities are small.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 14, 55; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation CALC-41; calculation CALC-56; calculation CALC-55

- No event after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet changes net debt in the sources read, so the net debt table carries no pro forma figure. The Grover price is stated four ways in the annual report, USD 850 million upfront, USD 858 million of cash after adjustments, USD 56 million of contingent consideration at fair value and USD 914 million in total, and the cash flow figure of USD 861 million is the one used for cash; up to USD 200 million more may be paid on revenue targets.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 141, 159–160; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 12; calculation CALC-52
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against the cautious reading is the trend: unadjusted net leverage fell from 4.60x to 4.24x in nine months, the issuer targets below 3.0x on its own measure in the first half of 2027, the revolver covenant is tested only when borrowings exceed 30% of commitments and USD 70 million of USD 1,000 million was drawn, and the issuer reports compliance with its financial covenants. That case wins if the legal and related add-backs fall back towards the USD 79 million of 2024, the fourth-quarter interest payment does not lift cash cover toward expense cover, and debt reduction continues at the third-quarter pace rather than yielding to share repurchases.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 169; calculation CALC-33

Three observations would change the view toward more caution: a rise in restructuring and other beyond the USD 244 million of the last twelve months, a draw on the revolver that approaches the covenant test, or no refinancing plan for the 2029 maturities by the time the Term Loan B becomes current in 2028.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 165–166; calculation CALC-32; calculation CALC-46
### Limitations

The statements are consolidated and no borrower-group, guarantor or restricted-group figures were supplied, so leverage cannot be read where the debt sits or the covenant is tested, and covenant headroom is not established.

The issuer prints no unadjusted EBITDA, so the base measure is calculated here and includes other income and the loss on debt financing; interim ratios use twelve-month figures built from unaudited stubs.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation CALC-8; calculation CALC-27
The maturity ladder is printed only at December 31, 2025, and statement lines that print a dash are carried as missing, not as zero.

## Gaps

- No executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied, so covenant definitions, baskets and the covenant EBITDA are not available and the first lien leverage covenant cannot be tested or its headroom stated; the debt terms in the debt table rest on the issuer's own note summary. Obtain the executed agreements and their amendments, including the January 22, 2026 repricing. Severity: High.

- The statements are consolidated and no separate financial information exists for the borrower, the guarantors or the restricted group, so leverage and cover cannot be read at the level where the debt sits and the revolver covenant is tested. Obtain guarantor or restricted-group financial information if the filer provides it. Severity: High.

- The maturity ladder is printed at December 31, 2025 and not at September 30, 2026, so the maturities chart and the principal reconciliation are drawn at year-end and do not show the USD 188 million of principal repaid since. Obtain the ladder at the latest date from the executed agreements or the next filing. Severity: Medium.

- The issuer prints no unadjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA (Reported) is calculated here from net income, tax, interest and depreciation, amortization and impairments, which keeps other income and loss on debt financing inside it; interim leverage and cover use twelve-month figures built from unaudited stubs. State the definition beside every ratio and prefer audited year-end columns for conclusions. Severity: Medium.

- Cash interest paid is timing-sensitive: the third quarter of 2026 shows USD 63 million against USD 89 million a year earlier, so cover on cash interest of 3.97x is higher than cover on interest expense of 3.48x. Read the two together until a full year of the 2033 notes' April and October coupons is in the data. Severity: Medium.

- The adjusted EBITDA add-backs are the issuer's own labels; restructuring and other includes legal and related costs of USD 79 million in 2024, USD 130 million in 2025 and USD 50 million in the first nine months of 2026, and the issuer states no realisation status for any add-back. Obtain the issuer's analysis of which costs it expects not to recur. Severity: Medium.

- The financing and investing lines that print a dash in a filing, for example the Q3 2026 loss on debt financing, the Q1 2026 exchange rate effect, the first-quarter and half-year 2026 treasury stock lines and several debt issuance and repayment lines, are carried as missing and not as zero, although the totals show they are nil; no later filing can change this. Severity: Low.

- Lines that a quarterly filing does not print, such as proceeds from notes and term loans in the first quarter, are shown as not printed; the annual statements itemise cash flow adjustments that the quarterly statements show in one line, so the annual columns carry calculated sums. Use the sums only for comparison with interim columns. Severity: Low.

- Per-share amounts, share counts, noncontrolling interest and discontinued operations are not carried in the statement tables, which state one unit of USD millions; they are in the filings if needed. Severity: Low.

- Operating indicator definitions, including average daily revenue per unit and the installed base inclusive of Grover, were revised in the fourth quarter of 2025, so indicators in the 2024 annual report are on the earlier basis. Use the revised comparatives. Severity: Low.

- The note maturity day and month, the interest rate floors, and the security and rank of USD 5 million of other debt are not stated in the pages read; the debt stack leaves the other debt out for that reason. Obtain the indentures and credit agreements. Severity: Low.

- The Q4 2025 quarter is not printed alone; the 2025 annual report gives only the year, so Q4 2025 would be the difference between FY2025 and the first nine months of 2025. The issuer's 2025 quarterly reports were not supplied, so 2025 interim figures are the comparatives printed in the 2026 reports. Severity: Low.

- No supplier finance, factoring, securitisation, customer deposit or deferred revenue arrangement was found in a search of all eight sources, so no non-debt funding float is flagged; contract liabilities are the only related balance and are small. Severity: Low.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Governance risk is medium: no sponsor or controlling holder is identified and no dividend has been paid, but USD 1,495 million of share repurchases since 2024 alongside a debt-funded acquisition show that shareholders compete with creditors for cash.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100, 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation CALC-15

Revenue is mostly recurring or leased, USD 1,555 million or 63.73% of nine-month revenue, which steadies cash flow, but social casino revenue is falling and three class actions are open. Repurchases stopped in the third quarter of 2026 in favour of debt reduction, and the test is whether they stay stopped as leverage nears the issuer's 3.0x target.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation CALC-6
### Key findings

- Ownership and control are not established, so sponsor behaviour is judged from actions and not from identity. The common stock has had its sole primary listing as depositary interests on the ASX since November 2025, no holder or board majority is named, and director and ownership information sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied; no fee, dividend or sponsor-led recapitalisation is evidenced, but no outside backstop is evidenced either.

- Financial policy has favoured shareholders alongside leverage, and willingness to pay out is shown more clearly than capacity. The issuer repurchased USD 462 million of shares in 2024, USD 877 million in 2025, including USD 500 million in the fourth quarter, and USD 156 million in the first nine months of 2026, while borrowing a USD 800 million Term Loan A to buy Grover. The debt agreements were not supplied, so how much more could be paid out is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 128, 166; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-12

- The 2026 pause in repurchases is real but discretionary. No shares were repurchased under the program in the third quarter, net revolver repayments were USD 160 million in nine months, and the issuer says it put deleveraging ahead of buybacks and aims for net debt leverage below 3.0x in the first half of 2027 on its own measure, from 3.3x at September 30, 2026. USD 180 million of program capacity remains, the program runs to June 12, 2027, and the employee share trust still bought USD 30 million of depositary interests in the quarter.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 21, 59; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 5; calculation CALC-11

- Refinancing has been creditor-aligned. The 2033 notes, at a coupon 0.75 percentage points below the 2028 notes they replaced, repaid those notes and the revolver in September 2025; the revolver was enlarged to USD 1.0 billion and extended to 2030, and the January 2026 Term Loan B margin cut saves about USD 5 million a year. The Term Loan B was also repriced twice in 2024, cutting its rate by 85 basis points in total. No exchange, priming or waiver is described, although the executed amendments were not supplied.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_lnw-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 127, 166, 167; 10-Q_2026-03-31_lnw-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 19; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_lnw03312026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation CALC-13

- The operating base is mostly recurring, but growth comes from leased machines and iGaming while digital and cyclical lines weaken. In the first nine months of 2026 gaming operations revenue rose 17.63% and iGaming 14.75%, while SciPlay fell 9.68%, machine sales fell 8.18% and systems fell 18.27%. Gaming earned a 54.91% segment adjusted EBITDA margin against 37.71% for SciPlay and 36.79% for iGaming, so Gaming provided 74.33% of segment adjusted EBITDA and group cash flow rests on the gaming machine business.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 15, 16, 17; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-7

- Exposure outside the United States is material, and receivables are more international than revenue. Customers outside the United States gave 31.50% of FY2025 revenue, and international receivables were 47.53% of the total at September 30, 2026.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 149; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-14

- Controls and legal exposure keep the risk from being low. The year-end internal-control assessment left out Grover, about 14% of total assets and 3% of net revenues, and two consumer class actions against SciPlay and a shareholder class action in Australia are open with no damages estimate; accrued legal liabilities fell by USD 90 million in nine months and USD 137 million of settlements were paid in the first quarter.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 131; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 36, 37, 40; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_lnw03312026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation CALC-10
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a medium rating is behavioural: no dividend has ever been paid, no liability management transaction is described, the 2033 refinancing cut the coupon, revolver borrowings were only USD 70 million against USD 1.0 billion of commitments, repurchases paused in the third quarter, and the issuer reports net debt leverage of 3.3x on its own measure, down from 3.4x. A proxy statement showing an independent board and no related-party dealings, together with tight restricted-payment limits in the executed agreements, would move the rating to low. It would move to high if repurchases resumed before the 3.0x target is reached, if another debt-funded acquisition followed Grover, or if an amendment loosened payment limits. Gaming machine sales also rose 5.29% in the third quarter after falling over nine months, which hints at a recovering replacement cycle for the business that carries group earnings.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100, 127, 169; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 21, 59; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-9
### Limitations

- No proxy statement was supplied, so board independence, holder percentages, insider holdings and related-party dealings are not established; the medium rating rests on actions and would be revisited if a controlling holder or fees to a holder were disclosed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135

- The executed credit agreements and indentures were not supplied, so the payment, investment and borrowing room left under the restricted-payment and debt limits is not established; willingness is read from what the issuer did, and capacity is not tested.

- The recurring share of revenue of 63.73% is a floor: systems maintenance and table rental revenue that the issuer also counts as recurring sits inside lines that are not separated, so durability is understated by an amount that cannot be measured.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation CALC-6
- The class action damages and the repurchase funding source are not stated, so the legal and financial policy conclusions give a direction and not a size.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Grover is the only acquisition in the period. It closed on May 16, 2025 for USD 850 million upfront, which the annual report values at USD 914 million of total consideration including USD 858 million of cash and USD 56 million of contingent consideration, with up to USD 200 million more payable on revenue targets. The proceeds of a USD 800 million Term Loan A, signed on May 15, 2025, were used to complete it, and it added leased charitable gaming units that raise recurring revenue and capital spending.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 160, 166; calculation CALC-12

The only new debt issue is the USD 1.0 billion of 2033 notes issued on September 24, 2025. Its USD 988 million of net proceeds redeemed the USD 700 million of 2028 notes and repaid revolver borrowings, and it cut the coupon by 0.75 percentage points. The revolver was enlarged to USD 1.0 billion and extended to 2030 in February 2025, the Term Loan B margin was cut in January 2026, and no new notes or term loans were issued in the first nine months of 2026, when revolver borrowings fell from USD 230 million to USD 70 million.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 127, 166, 167; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 21; calculation CALC-13

Capital returns run alongside these transactions. The repurchase program of USD 1.5 billion, raised from USD 1.0 billion on July 31, 2025, had USD 180 million of capacity left at September 30, 2026 and no repurchases in the third quarter, and the 2023 SciPlay minority buy-in cost USD 496 million in cash.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 145; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 5

## Gaps

- The 2026 proxy statement was not supplied, so holder percentages, board composition, committee structure, insider holdings and related-party dealings are not established. Obtain the proxy statement. Severity: High.

- The executed credit agreements, indentures and all four amendments were not supplied, so restricted-payment, investment, debt and lien capacity cannot be set against the repurchase and acquisition history, and the 2024 amendments are known only as the repricings the 2024 annual report summarises. Obtain the executed documents. Severity: High.

- The funding source of the repurchases, the stake acquired in Grover and the schedule for up to USD 200 million of contingent payments are not stated in the pages read. Read the cash flow commentary and the purchase accounting note in the next annual report. Severity: Medium.

- No customer concentration is disclosed in the pages read, so single-customer loss in the Gaming segment cannot be tested. Check the risk factors and customer notes in the next annual report. Severity: Medium.

- No guarantor and non-guarantor split of revenue, assets and liabilities was supplied, so the structural subordination of the notes cannot be sized. Obtain guarantor financial information if the issuer provides it. Severity: Medium.

- The class action damages are unquantified and accrued legal liabilities of USD 54 million at September 30, 2026 are the issuer's own estimate, so the legal cash cost is not bounded. Track accrual and settlement disclosure each quarter. Severity: Medium.

- The amended bylaws and the Corporate Governance Statement on the ASX announcements page were not supplied, so changes to shareholder and board rights since the listing move are not known. Obtain both documents. Severity: Low.

- The sources end with the quarterly report of November 4, 2026, so no event after September 30, 2026 is carried; the only later date is the share count at October 30, 2026. Re-read the next filing for subsequent events. Severity: Low.

# Fundamental credit for Light & Wonder, Inc. (lnwo-750004), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Fundamental credit for Light & Wonder, Inc. (lnwo-750004), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope: the issuer's business profile, cash flow, leverage, liquidity, refinancing capacity, financial policy and primary downside path, from the supplied filings and releases and the earlier module findings.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Fundamental credit quality is adequate but leveraged: recurring leased-machine and iGaming earnings and liquidity of USD 1,059 million support creditors, while unadjusted net leverage of 4.24x and USD 2,568 million of principal due in 2029 constrain them.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 165; calculation CALC-5

Net leverage is 3.3x on the issuer's adjusted measure and falling, but add-backs of USD 355 million, a shrinking social casino business, legal cash costs and discretionary repurchases could stall deleveraging. The primary downside path is a casino capital-spending pause that cuts machine sales while social casino keeps shrinking, ahead of the 2029 refinancing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 18; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-14
### Key findings

- The business profile is adequate: recurring and leased revenue anchors cash flow, but one segment carries most of it. Recurring or leased revenue was at least 63.73% of nine-month revenue, gaming operations revenue rose 17.63% and the North American premium installed base grew for a 25th consecutive quarter, and Gaming provided 74.33% of segment adjusted EBITDA. Leased units earn daily fees through the casino capital cycle, so they support debt service when machine sales fall, but group cash flow still depends on one segment and its customers' spending.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–17

- Earnings are growing faster than revenue, so margin and mix, not volume, carry the credit. Revenue for the twelve months to September 30, 2026 was 0.48% above FY2025 and Q3 revenue fell 2.02%, while adjusted EBITDA rose 3.81% to USD 1,498 million at a 44.98% margin, services revenue rose 5.90% and products revenue fell 11.51% in nine months. Selling, general and administrative costs fell to 26.22% of FY2025 revenue from 27.35%, but flat revenue leaves less room for margin gains to keep funding deleveraging.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 139; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-7; calculation CALC-8; calculation CALC-9

- Leverage is moderate on the issuer's measure and high on unadjusted earnings, so creditors should size the risk on the higher figure. Net debt was 4.24x unadjusted EBITDA and 3.3x on the issuer's adjusted measure at September 30, 2026, against 4.60x unadjusted at the end of 2025, and add-backs of USD 355 million are 23.70% of adjusted EBITDA. Legal and related costs inside the add-backs were USD 79 million in 2024, USD 130 million in 2025 and USD 179 million over the last twelve months, so they recur.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation CALC-5

- Cash flow covers scheduled debt service with room, and it does so after legal settlements. Operating cash flow less capital expenditures was USD 596 million over the last twelve months against scheduled 2026 principal and interest of USD 369 million, 1.62x, and USD 369 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 257 million a year earlier, after USD 137 million of settlements paid in the first quarter. Shareholder returns of USD 193 million in the nine months compete for the same cash, and capital spending of USD 339 million over twelve months absorbs part of operating cash flow before any debt repayment.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 18; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4

- Liquidity is strong, and the refinancing wall is the real test. Liquidity of USD 1,059 million is 1.23x the USD 859 million of principal due before 2029 on the year-end ladder, and revolver borrowings of USD 70 million sit far below the USD 300 million at which the revolver's 4.50x first lien test applies. Business & governance reads the maintenance test as inactive while the revolver is undrawn; that holds for the revolver only, because the Term Loan A carries the same test every quarter, and the issuer states compliance without printing a covenant figure. USD 2,568 million, 49.32% of principal, falls due in 2029, 59.06% of principal is variable rate, swaps of USD 700 million end in April 2027, and the issuer puts a 1% rate move at USD 30 million of interest before swaps. The 2033 notes show market access at a lower coupon, but no agency rating or market price was supplied.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 60, 165, 167, 169; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 22, 58; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-12; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-11

- Financial policy is the swing factor, and it has turned toward debt reduction for now. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk Medium: no sponsor or controlling holder is identified and no dividend has been paid, but repurchases were USD 1,495 million from 2024 to September 30, 2026. None were made in Q3 2026, USD 180 million of program capacity remains and the issuer aims for net debt leverage below 3.0x in the first half of 2027; the pause is a board choice and not a contractual limit.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 5

- Social casino, legal exposure and cyclical sales are the main earnings risks. SciPlay revenue fell 9.68% in nine months with fewer monthly active users and a lower payer conversion rate than a year earlier, gaming machine sales and systems fell 8.18% and 18.27% and together were 29.06% of revenue, and the issuer expects full-year adjusted EBITDA growth toward the lower end of a mid-to-high single digit range because of social casino weakness and delayed customer investment. Gaming machine sales rose 5.29% in the third quarter, three class actions are open and the UK online gambling duty rose to 40% from April 1, 2026.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 51; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation CALC-18
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a better view is deleveraging momentum and earnings quality: principal fell USD 188 million since year-end, the issuer's net debt leverage fell from 3.5x to 3.3x with a target below 3.0x in the first half of 2027, adjusted EBITDA rose 3.81%, the revolver is almost undrawn, and the 2033 notes refinanced at a lower coupon. That case wins if legal costs fall back toward the USD 79 million of 2024, social casino stabilises, the buyback pause holds and the 2029 maturities are addressed well before the Term Loan B nears maturity. The view would turn more cautious if revenue fell again after Q3, if revolver borrowings approached USD 300 million, if repurchases resumed before the target is met, or if a debt-funded acquisition followed Grover.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 5, 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation CALC-17; calculation CALC-7; calculation CALC-12
### Limitations

- The analysis of earnings changes and the peer comparison were not supplied, so margin durability rests on one year of reported segment margins and relative strength against sector peers is not established.
- No agency rating, bond price or loan trading level was supplied, so the view that refinancing capacity is adequate rests on the 2025 issuance and not on current market pricing.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 167; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 11

- The downside sensitivity is an illustrative 10% fall in adjusted EBITDA chosen by the analyst, with the whole shortfall taken to cash flow; it shows direction and not a forecast of stressed leverage.
Basis: calculation CALC-15; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 18

### Company description

Light & Wonder is a cross-platform games company with three segments: Gaming, which sells and leases machines, systems and table products and includes the Grover charitable gaming business; SciPlay, a social casino and casual games business; and iGaming, which supplies content and platforms to online operators. Revenue was USD 3,314 million in FY2025 and customers outside the United States gave 31.50% of it, which ties cash flow to casino capital budgets, consumer spending on mobile platforms and online gambling rules in several jurisdictions. Recurring or leased revenue supports visibility, while sales of machines and systems add cyclicality, so the model supports debt service capacity but not a steady growth path.

### Ownership and group structure

The company is publicly traded as depositary interests on the ASX since November 2025 and quoted over the counter in the United States; no sponsor or controlling holder is named, and holder percentages and board composition sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied. All reported debt sits in a wholly owned subsidiary, Light and Wonder International, Inc., guaranteed by the parent and by wholly owned domestic subsidiaries and secured on first-priority liens for the credit facilities, while the notes are senior unsecured and structurally behind the liabilities of non-guarantor subsidiaries, whose size is not disclosed. Without a sponsor, leverage tolerance is judged from actions: repurchases since 2024, a debt-funded acquisition and a pause in repurchases in the third quarter of 2026.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 62, 100, 169; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is driven by leased machine volumes and daily fees, new machine shipments, social casino payer numbers and iGaming wagers. Gaming operations revenue rose 17.63% and iGaming rose 14.75% in nine months while SciPlay fell 9.68% and machine sales fell 8.18%; services revenue, which carries the leased and digital lines, was 73.52% of revenue and rose 5.90% (calculation CALC-8). Revenue is therefore recurring and visible in the leased and iGaming lines, cyclical in machine and systems sales, and structurally declining in social casino so far; pricing power is shown only by a higher average sales price per new unit in Q3 2026, and no customer concentration is disclosed.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10, 14, 46, 51; calculation CALC-8
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs are largely fixed in the short run: selling, general and administrative costs were USD 869 million in FY2025 against USD 872 million in FY2024 while revenue rose 3.95%, research and development was 7.60% of revenue and depreciation, amortization and impairments 12.25% (calculation CALC-9). Operating leverage therefore helps when revenue grows and hurts when it falls, and cost of products fell {pct(483 - 436, 483)}% against a {pct(1083 - 1017, 1083)}% fall in products revenue, which cushions a cyclical downturn only in part. Margins can be defended under mild volume pressure, but a fall in machine sales with fixed costs would reduce margins faster than revenue. Tariffs and components sourced from China and Asia are a further cost risk the issuer is monitoring.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 41, 139; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10, 46; calculation CALC-9
### Capital intensity and cash flow conversion

Capital expenditures were USD 247 million in nine months, 10.12% of revenue, of which Gaming USD 201 million, and operating cash flow was 64.71% of unadjusted EBITDA for nine months against 73.18% in FY2025 (calculation CALC-10), so conversion is good but lower in the period with the settlements. Operating cash flow less capital expenditures was USD 596 million over twelve months (calculation CALC-2), enough to cover scheduled 2026 principal and interest of USD 369 million 1.62x (calculation CALC-4). Gaming operations need heavy up-front capital, so growth in leased units lowers free cash flow before it raises it, and capital spending can be slowed to protect cash if needed, at the cost of installed base growth.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 17, 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 126, 141–142; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-4
### Porter's Five Forces, credit-translated

Rivalry is intense in every segment: the issuer names Aristocrat, IGT and Konami in machines and systems, Playtika and others in social casino and Evolution, Pragmatic Play and Playtech in iGaming, so share losses in a segment hit pricing and the margin that supports debt service. New entrants are a threat mainly in social casino, which the issuer calls a business with low barriers to entry, so SciPlay's margin is the least protected. Substitutes are other forms of play and leisure that compete for player time, which pressures social casino user numbers.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12–15, 46

Casino operators hold buyer power because they set replacement cycles through their capital budgets, and consolidation among operators could shift purchases to competitors, although repeat customers are a substantial part of Gaming revenue. Supplier power sits with app store platforms, whose payment processing fees sit in cost of services, and with Asian component suppliers exposed to tariffs; the direct-to-consumer route reached 28.84% of SciPlay revenue against 17.20% a year earlier, which reduces platform dependence and supports the segment margin.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 13, 41, 56, 153; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14
### PEST factors

Regulation and tax matter for credit: the UK online gambling duty rose to 40% from April 1, 2026, which lowers customer spend in iGaming, US tariffs could raise component costs, and consumer-protection law is the basis of the class actions against SciPlay. Economic conditions drive casino capital budgets and consumer spending, and variable-rate debt of 59.06% of principal makes rates a direct cost driver, while customers outside the United States gave 31.50% of revenue. Technology matters through platform rules and iGaming growth, with USD 31.7 billion of wagers processed in Q3 2026.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 34, 41, 149; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36, 37, 54; calculation CALC-11
### SWOT, credit-translated

Strengths: recurring leased and iGaming earnings, large liquidity, a single first lien covenant and market access shown by the 2033 notes. Weaknesses: leverage that is high on unadjusted earnings, a concentrated 2029 maturity wall, a shrinking social casino business and cyclical machine sales. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are growth in the premium installed base and Grover units, iGaming growth and meeting the leverage target below 3.0x. Threats that could weaken it are customer delays in capital spending, higher legal costs, higher duties on online gambling and a return to repurchases before the target is met.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 5
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

In the next 12 to 24 months the issuer expects full-year adjusted EBITDA growth toward the lower end of a mid-to-high single digit range, a seasonally strong fourth quarter and net debt leverage toward 3.0x by the end of FY2026 and below it in the first half of 2027; scheduled principal is small at USD 53 million in 2026 and USD 63 million in 2027, and the swaps end in April 2027. Tailwinds are installed base growth, Grover expansion and iGaming content; headwinds are social casino weakness, delayed customer investment, legal settlements and higher duties. Over three to five years the Term Loan A of USD 720 million in 2028 and USD 2,568 million in 2029 become the test: with variable-rate debt of 59.06% of principal, refinancing cost depends on reaching the target before then.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 165; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58; calculation CALC-11
### Downside scenario

A realistic downside starts with casino operators delaying capital spending, which the issuer already cites, while social casino keeps shrinking at the nine-month pace. Gaming machine sales and systems, 29.06% of revenue, fall first, and fixed costs turn that into a faster fall in adjusted EBITDA; a 10% fall in adjusted EBITDA would lift the issuer's leverage ratio to 3.62x and unadjusted net leverage to 4.88x (calculation CALC-15). Cash flow after capital expenditures would still cover scheduled 2026 debt service 1.21x even if the whole shortfall reached cash, liquidity of USD 1,059 million would remain above the USD 859 million of principal due before 2029, and the revolver's test would apply only after borrowings pass USD 300 million, although the Term Loan A test applies every quarter and its headroom is not established. Management levers are pausing repurchases, slowing capital spending and timing legal settlements, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis, and the pressure falls on refinancing the 2028 and 2029 maturities at a higher spread if leverage stays above the target when the hedge has ended.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 40; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-12; calculation CALC-13
### Overall credit view

Overall, Light & Wonder presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring leased and iGaming earnings, large liquidity and a stated priority on deleveraging, but credit quality is constrained by leverage that is high on unadjusted earnings, a concentrated 2029 maturity wall and discretionary shareholder returns. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: operating cash flow less capital expenditures covers scheduled debt service 1.62x after legal settlements. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on reaching the leverage target before the 2028 and 2029 maturities and on market conditions when the swaps end. The primary downside path is a casino capital-spending pause with continued social casino decline, followed by weaker earnings against a concentrated maturity wall. Further analysis would require the executed debt agreements, the proxy statement, guarantor information, agency ratings, market pricing and a peer comparison. Top risk: refinancing the 2029 maturities if deleveraging stalls.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-11
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength: recurring leased and iGaming earnings give creditors visibility. Gaming operations revenue rose 17.63% and the premium installed base grew for a 25th consecutive quarter, and recurring or leased revenue was at least 63.73% of revenue; daily lease fees continue through casino capital cycles, so debt service does not depend on new machine orders.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14

Strength: liquidity is large and the covenant package is a single first lien test. Liquidity of USD 1,059 million covers the principal due before 2029 1.23x, and the revolver's test applies only if borrowings pass USD 300 million against USD 70 million drawn, so a cash shortfall can be absorbed without a revolver covenant event; the Term Loan A carries the same 4.50x test every quarter and compliance is stated.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 60, 167, 169; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 22; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-12

Strength: cash flow after capital spending covers debt service and deleveraging is under way. Operating cash flow less capital expenditures was USD 596 million over twelve months against USD 369 million of scheduled 2026 debt service, and principal fell USD 188 million since year-end, so repayment is coming from cash flow and not from new borrowing.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_lnw-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-17

Strength: financial policy shows no extraction by a sponsor. No controlling holder or sponsor is identified, no dividend has been paid, refinancing cut the coupon and the third quarter of 2026 put debt reduction ahead of repurchases, which lowers the risk that cash is diverted from creditors.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 5

Weakness: leverage is high on unadjusted earnings and the issuer's lower figure leans on add-backs. Net debt was 4.24x unadjusted EBITDA against 3.3x on the issuer's measure, with add-backs of USD 355 million that include recurring legal costs, so a creditor servicing debt in cash carries more leverage than the headline.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation CALC-5

Weakness: the maturity wall in 2029 is concentrated and mostly floating. USD 2,568 million, 49.32% of principal, falls due in one year with 59.06% of principal at variable rates and swaps of USD 700 million ending in April 2027, so refinancing cost and timing depend on markets and on reaching the leverage target.

Weakness: social casino is shrinking and legal exposure is growing. SciPlay revenue fell 9.68% with fewer active and paying users, and three class actions are open while USD 137 million of settlements were paid in the first quarter, so a second earnings pillar weakens as a cash claim rises.

Weakness: machine and systems sales are cyclical and customers are delaying spending. These lines were 29.06% of nine-month revenue and fell 8.18% and 18.27%, and the issuer cites delayed customer investment in its outlook, so earnings outside leased units can fall faster than revenue when casino budgets tighten.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lnw-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lnw09302026erandtables.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation CALC-18

Weakness: shareholder returns remain discretionary. Repurchases of USD 1,495 million since 2024 were made while acquisition debt was being added, and the pause since the third quarter is a board choice with USD 180 million of capacity left, so the pace of deleveraging can change quickly.

## Gaps

- No agency rating, bond price or loan trading level was supplied, so refinancing capacity is read from the 2025 issuance and not from current pricing. Obtain current ratings and trading levels. Severity: Medium.

- The earnings-change analysis and the peer benchmark were not supplied, so the margin trend rests on reported statements and no comparison with sector peers is available. Obtain both before a final committee view. Severity: Medium.

- The executed credit agreements were not supplied, so the covenant definitions, the covenant EBITDA, the reported first lien leverage figure and the conditions of the Term Loan A test are not available and headroom is not established for either test. Obtain the executed agreements and any compliance certificate. Severity: High.

- The maturity ladder is printed only at December 31, 2025 and scheduled 2026 payments use December 31, 2025 rates, while the rate floors and the hedge position after the swaps end in April 2027 are not stated, so interest cost beyond early 2027 cannot be projected. Obtain the ladder and hedge terms at the latest date. Severity: Medium.

- Capital expenditure is split by segment only, Gaming USD 201 million of USD 247 million in nine months, and not between maintenance and growth or leased units, so capital spending flexibility cannot be sized. Obtain the capital expenditure split from the issuer. Severity: Medium.

- The effect of the UK online gambling duty rise to 40% on iGaming earnings is not quantified, and the issuer gives no fourth-quarter or FY2027 figures beyond the lower end of a range. Track the next release. Severity: Low.
